core_obligations: Set up the exact functor given by the total tensor product between the homotopy category of R and the derived category of A (proof lines 14679-14685).
Verify the two hypotheses of the existence lemma for the class of K-flat complexes, so that the derived functor is everywhere defined (proof lines 14686-14715).
Record that the derived functor is computed by K-flat resolutions and reuse that in the base-change computation (proof lines 14716-14720).
Compute both sides of the base-change isomorphism on a K-flat representative, using that base change preserves K-flatness (proof lines 14721-14725).
proof_roadmap: Name the functor and set up the derived-functor situation (proof lines 14679-14690).
Check existence via K-flat complexes (proof lines 14691-14715).
Identify the derived functor with the explicit total tensor product on K-flat complexes (proof lines 14716-14720).
Verify the base-change isomorphism by direct computation (proof lines 14721-14725).
difficulty_reason: The lemma records two properties of the derived tensor product constructed in the preceding text: that the construction is independent of choices and defines an exact functor of triangulated categories, and that it satisfies a functorial base-change isomorphism. The proof is an application of the general machinery of right derived functors: the author sets up the homotopy category and the derived category, names the exact functor given by taking the total tensor product, checks the two hypotheses of the existence lemma for the class of K-flat complexes, and concludes that the derived functor is everywhere defined and computed by K-flat resolutions. The final isomorphism is then verified by computing both sides on a K-flat representative, using that base change of a K-flat complex is again K-flat and that the two total complex constructions agree.
